description: Partner-ingest QA contracts for validating raw Fintech Sandbox and aggregator payloads before they are normalized into the Ventus enrichment input contract.

plaid_transactions_sync.amount_sign_convention: Plaid positive values mean money moved out of the account; negative values mean money moved in. Normalization must map this to Ventus transaction_type without flipping merchant-spend semantics.

rail_rules.card: Use for card purchase, in-store, online, and POS-like merchant activity.
rail_rules.ach: Use for payroll, direct deposit, recurring debit, loan payment, or bank transfer activity.
rail_rules.p2p: Use for Zelle, Venmo-like, payment_app, or person-to-person transfer counterparties.
rail_rules.wire: Use for wire-like title, escrow, international, or large transfer activity when the raw description supports it.

qa_gates: Every added or modified transaction maps to exactly one normalized transaction unless explicitly excluded.
Every normalized transaction has a bank customer mapping and home ZIP before enrichment.
Pending-to-posted changes keep source_transaction_id lineage through partner_metadata.
Removed transactions are not sent to enrichment as new transactions.
Payroll, refunds, and credits are not evaluated as consumer spend.

generic_fintech_sandbox_partner.amount_sign_convention: Partner-specific. The raw payload must specify either signed amounts or explicit debit/credit direction before normalization.

rail_rules.card: Use when the source identifies card or POS purchase activity.
rail_rules.ach: Use when the source identifies ACH, direct deposit, external transfer, subscription, or loan payment activity.
rail_rules.bill_pay: Use when the source identifies bank bill-pay payee records.
rail_rules.merchant_integration: Use for CRM, offer, loyalty, or merchant-side signals that are not financial postings.

qa_gates: Raw direction semantics are documented before normalization.
Every raw account maps to a bank customer or is explicitly rejected.
Partner-specific optional fields are preserved under partner_metadata.
Normalization failures produce a reject report, not silent drops.
